key_cases.case_name: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare v. Doe (2016-11)
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination, the court held that the Department satisfied I.C. § 16-1621(3)(c) by developing four case plans identifying the issues, the parent's tasks and the Department's own role, and that substantial and competent evidence supported the findings of neglect, inability to discharge parental responsibilities, and best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Specifies what an adequate Idaho case plan must contain: the issues, the parent's tasks, and the Department's stated role.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the magistrate court did not err by finding that the IDHW made reasonable efforts to reunify Mother with her children

key_cases.case_name: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare v. Doe
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination, the court held that the Department's reunification efforts and its placement choices are CPA requirements that are not relevant to whether the statutory grounds for termination are proved, and that the mother's due-process rights were protected by the clear-and-convincing burden at the termination trial.
key_cases.relevance: Draws the line lawyers most often miss: reasonable-efforts findings belong to the CPA case and must be contested there, not on the termination appeal.
key_cases.quote: those cases also demonstrate that such findings are irrelevant to termination proceedings because reasonable efforts are requirements under the CPA, not Idaho's parental-rights termination statute

key_cases.case_name: In re Termination of the Parental Rights of Jane (2013-15) Doe
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination on neglect grounds, holding that neglect is a question of fact to be established by clear and convincing evidence, that substantial and competent evidence supported the aggravated-circumstances finding, and that the mother's due-process challenge to being relieved of a case plan was inadequately argued.
key_cases.relevance: An aggravated-circumstances finding lawfully ends the Department's duty to offer a reunification case plan.
key_cases.quote: Whether neglect has occurred is a question of fact to be established by clear and convincing evidence

key_cases.holding: The court vacated a termination order and remanded, holding that the rebuttable presumption in I.C. § 16-1629(9) favors only the Department's filing of a termination petition after fifteen of twenty-two months in care and does not shift to the parent the burden of disproving that termination is in the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: A parent's failure to complete services within the statutory window does not convert into a presumption against the parent at trial.
key_cases.quote: It does not create a presumption that it is in the best interests of the child to terminate parental rights

key_cases.case_name: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare v. Doe
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination as to both parents, the court held that I.C. § 16-1624 authorizes the Department to petition for termination once the court has found CPA jurisdiction at the adjudicatory hearing and placed the child in the Department's legal custody or protective supervision, so neither due process nor the termination statute's purpose provision requires that the parent first be given a full opportunity to complete a case plan.
key_cases.relevance: Rejects the argument that a parent must first be given a full opportunity to complete a CPA case plan before the Department may petition to terminate.
key_cases.quote: Thus, under the authority granted by the CPA, the Department is authorized to petition for termination if the court has jurisdiction over the child under the CPA

timeline_requirements.deadline: 48 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child taken into shelter care by a peace officer
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Child may be held no longer; release is required unless a shelter care hearing has been held and the court has ordered an adjudicatory hearing (Idaho Code § 16-1608(2))

notice_requirements.timing: At least twenty-four (24) hours before the shelter care hearing (Idaho Code § 16-1615(2))
content_required: That the person is entitled to be represented by legal counsel
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Notice must be given by personal service and the return of service filed with the court, except where the undelivered notice is returned to the court with an affidavit stating the parents or custodian could not be located or were out of the state (Idaho Code § 16-1615(3)); the shelter care hearing may be continued for a reasonable time upon request by the parent, custodian, or counsel for the child (§ 16-1615(4)). No other consequence is specified in Idaho Code § 16-1615
